task.title: Commits in the portfolio project
task.description: Git is configured, and you are in the ~/portfolio folder: it has a repository and a README.md file, there are no commits yet. Write the commands one per line: 1) Check the state of the repository, add README.md to the index and make the first commit. 2) Create index.html from several lines of HTML with cat > index.html << 'EOF' (the last line is EOF). 3) Create style.css with one CSS rule using echo. 4) Make a commit that contains only index.html. 5) Save style.css in a separate commit. 6) Append a line with a project description to README.md (with >>) and commit it with git commit -am. 7) Make sure the working directory is clean. Commit messages are in English, in the imperative mood, and each commit has its own (not "update" and not "commit").
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Git is configured, you are in the ~/portfolio folder. It has README.md and no commits.

# 1. Check the state, add README.md to the index and make the first commit

# 2. Create index.html of several lines: cat > index.html << 'EOF' ... EOF

# 3. Create style.css with echo

# 4. A commit with index.html only

# 5. A separate commit with style.css

# 6. Append a line to README.md (>>) and commit it with git commit -am

# 7. Check that the working directory is clean

tests.name: The repository has exactly 4 commits
tests.fail: You need 4 commits: README.md, index.html, style.css and the README.md edit. Check git log --oneline: was there a "nothing added to commit" error?

tests.name: The first commit contains only README.md
tests.fail: The first commit is git add README.md and git commit -m "..." before you create index.html and style.css.

tests.name: The second commit added only index.html
tests.fail: Before the second commit, add only index.html to the index: git add index.html, not git add .

tests.name: index.html has several lines
tests.fail: Create index.html with cat > index.html << 'EOF', several lines of HTML and the EOF line at the end.

tests.name: The third commit added style.css and did not change other files
tests.fail: The third commit: git add style.css, then git commit -m "...".

tests.name: style.css is not empty
tests.fail: For example: echo "body { font-family: sans-serif; }" > style.css

tests.name: The fourth commit changed only README.md
tests.fail: Append a line to README.md and run git commit -am "..." - only the modified README.md will go into the commit.

tests.name: The line was appended to README.md, not replacing it
tests.fail: Append with two signs: echo "..." >> README.md. A single > erases the old text.

tests.name: Commit messages are meaningful
tests.fail: Write what was done: "Add home page", "Add styles". The messages "update" and "commit" explain nothing.

tests.name: All commit messages are different
tests.check: repo !== null && new Set(repo.log().map((c) => c.subject.trim())).size === repo.log().length
tests.fail: Each commit has its own message - about what was done in that commit.

tests.name: The last commit was made with git commit -am
tests.fail: For an edit of the already tracked README.md: git commit -am "Describe project in README"

tests.name: The working directory is clean at the end
tests.fail: At the end git status must answer: nothing to commit, working tree clean.

tests.name: A different README.md: the first commit keeps the original text
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.log().length >= 1 && (repo.log().slice().reverse()[0].files["README.md"] ?? "") === "# Anna Karimova - works\n"
tests.fail: Do not overwrite README.md before the first commit: it already has text.

tests.name: A different README.md: the old line is kept after >>
tests.check: repo !== null && repo.log().length >= 4 && (repo.log().slice().reverse()[3].files["README.md"] ?? "").startsWith("# Anna Karimova - works\n") && (repo.log().slice().reverse()[3].files["README.md"] ?? "").split("\n").length >= 3
tests.fail: echo "..." >> README.md appends a line to the end. With > the old text is lost.

tests.name: The script ran without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes in the commands and the EOF line.

hints: The cycle is always the same: change files → git add file → git commit -m "Message".
A multi-line file: the first line is cat > index.html << 'EOF', then the HTML lines, the last line is EOF.
To get only index.html into the commit, add it by name: git add index.html. Check git status -s: A in the first column means it is in the index, ?? means it is not.
git commit -am does not take new files: style.css must be added with git add.
Append a line: echo "text" >> README.md (two > signs).
Example messages: Add README, Add home page, Add styles, Describe project in README.

questions.question: In which area of Git is a file right after git add but before git commit?
options: In the working directory and nowhere else
In the index (staging area)
In the repository, in the commit history
On GitHub
questions.explanation: git add puts a snapshot of the file into the index - the "box" of the next commit. It gets into the history after git commit.

questions.question: Match the state of a file with its description.
pairs: A new file that Git is not watching yet
The changes are added to the index and will go into the next commit
The version is saved in a commit, there are no changes
A tracked file has changed, but the changes are not in the index
questions.explanation: The life cycle: untracked → (git add) staged → (git commit) committed → (edit) modified → (git add) staged...

questions.question: git status -s shows the line "?? style.css". What does it mean?
options: The file is changed and added to the index
The file is new and not tracked
The file is deleted
The file has a conflict
questions.explanation: Two question marks mean untracked: Git sees the file, but it has never been added with git add.

questions.question: Match the git status -s line with its meaning.
pairs: A new file is added to the index
The file is changed, the changes are not in the index
The file's changes are added to the index
Some changes are in the index, the file was changed again after git add
questions.explanation: The left column is the index, the right one is the working directory. A space means "no changes here".

questions.question: Which commit messages are good according to the course rules?
options: Add contact form
update
Fix menu on small screens
I changed some stuff in the files and also the styles
commit
questions.explanation: A good message is in English, in the imperative mood, up to 50 characters, and says what was done.

questions.question: The folder has a new file about.html (never added) and a modified README.md. What will git commit -am "Add about page" do?
options: Commit both files
Commit only README.md, about.html stays untracked
Commit only about.html
Show an error and do nothing
questions.explanation: -a adds only files that are already tracked. A new file must be added with git add first.

questions.question: The README.md file has one line. Which redirection sign appends a new line to the end without erasing the old one? Enter only the sign.
questions.explanation: > overwrites the file, >> appends to the end.

questions.question: Git answered git commit -m "Add styles" with "nothing added to commit but untracked files present". What is the reason?
options: The commit message is too short
The index is empty: the new file was not added with git add
There is no repository
The style.css file is empty
questions.explanation: A commit takes only what is in the index. First run git add style.css.

questions.question: What is true about the git add . command?
options: It adds all new and modified files of the current folder and its subfolders to the index
It creates a commit right away
The dot means "the current folder"
It adds only files that are already in commits
questions.explanation: git add . puts all changes in the current folder into the index. The commit is made with a separate command.

questions.question: Complete the first line of the command that creates the index.html file from several lines (the input ends with the EOF line): cat > index.html ________
questions.explanation: cat > index.html << 'EOF' - everything up to the EOF line goes into the file. The quotes around EOF stop the shell from substituting variables like $USER.

questions.question: Git printed: "[main 7154fc6] Add styles / 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+) / create mode 100644 style.css". What does 7154fc6 mean?
options: A line number in the file
The short hash - the ID of the new commit
The file size
The repository password
questions.explanation: Every commit has a unique hash, and Git shows its first 7 characters. More in lesson 3.

questions.question: Why do we need the index if we could commit all changes at once?
options: The index speeds up the internet
To put into one commit only what belongs to one task
The index stores passwords
git status does not work without the index
questions.explanation: The index is a box where you put only what you need. This way one logical change = one commit.
